mcqs.learning_point: Understand the cell as the basic unit of life
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines a cell as the basic structural and functional unit of life?

options.A: A cell is the smallest living unit that can carry out all life processes independently.
options.B: A cell is a group of tissues that perform a specific function.
options.C: A cell is a non‑living particle that forms part of an organism.
options.D: A cell is only a storage compartment for genetic material.

mcqs.answer: A cell is the smallest living unit that can carry out all life processes independently.
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly states that a cell is the smallest unit capable of performing all life processes on its own, which is the definition of the basic unit of life. Option B describes a tissue, not a cell. Option C incorrectly calls a cell non‑living. Option D limits the cell to genetic storage, ignoring its many functions.

mcqs.learning_point: State the basic ideas of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which set of statements correctly states the three fundamental ideas of the cell theory?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of cells; cells are the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: Cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter; plants have cells, animals do not; cells are the smallest particles of matter.
options.C: Only multicellular organisms have cells; cells are only structural; cells can be created de novo.
options.D: Cells are the basic unit of life but do not arise from other cells; all organisms are made of tissues only.

mcqs.answer: All living organisms are composed of cells; cells are the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: Option A lists the three universally accepted statements of the cell theory. Options B, C, and D contain incorrect or contradictory statements such as spontaneous generation, exclusion of animals, or denial of the 'all cells arise from pre‑existing cells' principle.

mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms is an example of a multicellular organism?
mcqs.explanation: A mushroom is made up of many specialized cells, fitting the definition of a multicellular organism. Options A, B, and D are all unicellular organisms that perform all life processes within a single cell.

mcqs.question: A plant cell is observed to have a large central vacuole, numerous chloroplasts, and a rigid cell wall. Which function is most directly supported by these structures?

options.A: Photosynthesis and storage of water and nutrients

mcqs.answer: Photosynthesis and storage of water and nutrients
mcqs.explanation: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, the central vacuole stores water and nutrients, and the cell wall provides structural support. The other options describe functions not associated with these plant‑cell structures.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the cell as the basic unit of life
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about cells?

options.B: Cells are the basic unit of life.
options.C: Different cell types have structures suited to their functions.
options.D: Cells can arise only from pre‑existing cells.

mcqs.explanation: Prokaryotic cells (e.g., bacteria) lack a true nucleus, so the statement in option A is a misconception. Options B, C, and D are accurate statements about cells.

mcqs.learning_point: State the basic ideas of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the statements of the cell theory?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells.
options.B: All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.C: Cells are the basic unit of structure and function in living organisms.
options.D: Cells can be created spontaneously from non‑living matter.

mcqs.answer: Cells can be created spontaneously from non‑living matter.
mcqs.explanation: Option D describes the disproven idea of spontaneous generation, which is not part of modern cell theory. Options A, B, and C are the three core tenets of the theory.

mcqs.question: Which pair of statements correctly compares unicellular and multicellular organisms?

options.A: Unicellular organisms perform all life processes within a single cell, whereas multicellular organisms have specialized cells that perform different functions.
options.B: Unicellular organisms have specialized tissues, while multicellular organisms lack specialization.
options.C: Both unicellular and multicellular organisms have identical metabolic rates per cell.
options.D: Multicellular organisms can reproduce only sexually, whereas unicellular organisms reproduce only asexually.

mcqs.answer: Unicellular organisms perform all life processes within a single cell, whereas multicellular organisms have specialized cells that perform different functions.
mcqs.explanation: Option A accurately captures the key distinction: single‑cell life versus division of labor among many cells. Options B, C, and D contain incorrect statements about tissue specialization, metabolic rates, and modes of reproduction.

mcqs.question: In a nerve cell (neuron), which organelle is most directly involved in the rapid transmission of electrical impulses along the axon?
mcqs.explanation: The myelin sheath insulates the axon and allows saltatory conduction, greatly increasing impulse speed. Mitochondria provide energy, ribosomes synthesize proteins, and the nucleus contains genetic material, but none directly speed up impulse transmission.
